heading: EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

REGENT OF SEMARANG

CENTRAL JAVA PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Semarang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Semarang Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regent is the Regent of Semarang.
6. Regional Work Unit in charge hereinafter referred to as SKPD in charge is a Regional Work Unit that has main duties and functions in accordance with the related field.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gifts that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.

heading: CHAPTER II
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 3

Women's Empowerment and Protection is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. best interests of women.

heading: Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:
a. to empower women both individually and in groups and society at large so that they are able to live more independently; and
b. to prevent and address the risks of violence and vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled according to the principles of equality and justice.

heading: CHAPTER IV
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 6

1. The Regional Government has obligations and responsibilities for women's empowerment and protection.
2. Efforts for women's empowerment and protection as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Efforts for women's empowerment and protection as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 7

Women's empowerment is directed to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in the fields of:
a. economy;
b. social culture;
c. politics; and
d. law.

heading: Article 8
Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The empowerment of women in the political field as referred to in Article 7 letter c shall include:
a. involvement of women in decision-making at various levels;
b. provision of opportunities for women to hold public office;
c. participation in general elections; and
d. self-development through organizations to associate, assemble and express opinions.
2. The empowerment of women in the political field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. The empowerment of women in the legal field as referred to in Article 7 letter d shall include:
a. enhancement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services;
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
2. The empowerment of women in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 12

1. The protection of women shall include:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection;
c. legal protection.
2. Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of a decent standard of living.
3. Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
4. Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

heading: Article 14
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Elderly Women

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The implementation of protection for elderly women as referred to in Article 13 letter b is in order to extend life expectancy so that they can carry out their social functions and play an active role naturally in their social life.
2. Elderly women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive the right to protection for:
a. basic health services to maintain and improve health status including gerontological/geriatric services;
b. use of facilities and accessibility of public facilities and infrastructure; and
c. government administration services.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Women with Disabilities

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. The implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 13 letter c is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive the right to protection for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as the utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility to information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Homeless Women

heading: Article 17
Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Domestic Women Workers

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The implementation of protection for domestic women workers as referred to in Article 13 letter e is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
2. Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions;
b. health and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

heading: Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Women Heads of Household

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. The implementation of protection for women heads of household as referred to in Article 13 letter f is in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of household.
2. Women heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive the right to protection for:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as the economic support of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as head of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

heading: Part Eight
translated_text:
Part Eight

Women Former Residents of Correctional Institutions

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. The implementation of protection for women former residents of correctional institutions as referred to in Article 13 letter g is in order to provide protection from obstacles to adjusting in community life, so that they can carry out life normally.
2. Women former residents of correctional institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection for:
a. social rehabilitation and reintegration; and
b. opportunities to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

heading: Part Ninth
translated_text:
Part Ninth

Women Victims of Disaster

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. Implementation of Protection for women victims of disaster as referred to in Article 13 letter h in order to provide protection during disaster and post-disaster.
2. Women victims of disaster as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. access to proper housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

heading: Part Tenth
translated_text:
Part Tenth

Commercial Sex Workers

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

1. Implementation of Protection for commercial sex workers as referred to in Article 13 letter i in order to provide health protection and improvement of life skills as capital to improve social status.
2. Protection for commercial sex workers as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. providing life skills;
b. facilitating reproductive health services; and
c. preventing human trafficking.

heading: Part Eleventh
translated_text:
Part Eleventh

Women Victims of Violence

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. Implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j in order to provide legal protection and/or health recovery.
2. Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance after the occurrence of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. health services.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND

PROTECTION STRATEGY

Article 24

1. Women empowerment and protection is implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.
2. In women empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services are established as stipulated by Regent's Decree.
3. Women empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Agency handling Women's Empowerment.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

MECHANISM FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN EMPOWERMENT

AND PROTECTION

Article 25

The mechanism for implementation of women empowerment and protection is carried out through stages:
a. formulation of policy planning for programs and activities;
b. budgeting of programs and activities;
c. implementation of programs and activities; and
d. monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Formulation of policy planning for programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter a is implemented through:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of planning preparation for programs and activities with related SKPD; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. Formulation of policy planning for programs and activities is further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
3. Formulation of policy planning for programs and activities for implementation of women empowerment and protection is coordinated by the SKPD in charge of regional development planning.
4. Budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter b is implemented through general budget policy set forth in APBD.
5. Implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter c is implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities set forth in SKPD budget documents; and
b. coordination and synchronization of implementation of programs and activities with related SKPD.
6. Implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in Article 25 letter d is implemented through:
a. conducting periodic monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of programs and activities that have been carried out; and
b. making periodic reports.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FINANCING

Article 27

All costs for Implementation of policy planning for programs and activities related to Women Empowerment and Protection are sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. Other sources that are legal and non-binding.

heading: CHAPTER XII
CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 29

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all provisions of regional laws and regulations related to the Implementation of Women Empowerment and Protection that have existed so far, remain in force as long as they are not contrary to the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Semarang Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY

NUMBER 1 YEAR 2015 CONCERNING WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual by seeking to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women that causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in some discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so as not to experience violence and can live a decent life in accordance with the principles of humanity, equality and justice.

Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To carry out these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Semarang Regency Government as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Semarang Regency, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations in order to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Semarang Regency.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various development sectors, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

heading: Article 16

Article 16

Women with disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their activities and social interactions normally.

heading: Article 17
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 17

Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.

heading: Article 18
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 18

Domestic Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to perform household work in return for wages.

heading: Article 19
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 19

Women Heads of Households are women who, for various reasons, are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.

heading: Article 20
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 20

Women former inmates of correctional institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.

heading: Article 21
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 21

Women disaster victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.

Post-disaster recovery includes psychological services for victims, health services, residential facilities, facilitation of public facilities and infrastructure and economic access recovery as well as population data services and legal aid.

heading: Article 22
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 22

Women commercial sex workers are women who work as sex workers of their own volition and/or are prostituted.
Improving life skills for commercial sex workers is intended to provide additional knowledge through training and skills in accordance with the talents and abilities possessed so that they can live more independently and obtain decent work to improve their standard of living and change their social status so as not to become commercial sex workers because such work is not legalized.

The protection of commercial sex workers in this Regional Regulation is not intended to legalize the existence of commercial sex workers, but to provide protection to the commercial sex workers concerned in various sectors.

PUG is a strategy that can reduce gender gaps to achieve gender equality by using a gender perspective in the development process, women's empowerment is an affirmative strategy to achieve gender equality aimed at increasing the fulfillment of women's rights to protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
